summary.name: Claude Code Best Practices
summary.one_liner: Anthropic's official guide to working effectively with Claude Code, covering CLAUDE.md, verification checks, hooks, permissions, model/effort settings, and subagent and cost management.
use_cases: writing a concise CLAUDE.md for a repository
enforcing project rules with hooks instead of prompts
blocking Claude from reading secret files like .env
controlling token cost and context size in long sessions
setting up verification checks so Claude can test its own work
choosing permission modes and model effort levels
summary.what_it_does: The page is a documentation guide on using Claude Code well. It explains the difference between non-deterministic instructions (prompts, CLAUDE.md, skills) that the model interprets and deterministic controls (hooks, deny rules, managed settings) that the harness always applies. It advises keeping CLAUDE.md short, scoping rules with paths filters, putting team procedures in skills, and giving Claude a test or check to run so it can verify its own work. It also covers permission rules and the sandbox, auto mode and permission modes, effort levels, subagent usage, and cost controls such as /clear, /compact, and /usage.
notable: Separates instructions the model may ignore (CLAUDE.md, prompts) from hooks and deny rules that Claude Code enforces every time
Stop hook can block Claude from finishing until a typecheck or test passes
Covers cost controls like prompt cache timing, /usage breakdowns, and subagent model choice
Lists the Anthropic-recommended approach to permissions, sandboxing, and auto mode
caveats: Some features depend on plan or provider, such as /usage breakdowns and prompt cache duration
Permission deny rules match tool calls rather than intent, so a WebFetch deny does not block curl unless the sandbox is on
Auto mode is a model classifier and is not deterministic; deny rules are needed for guarantees
